mechaber/1:main: Your table should be set from the daytime, in order to eat right away when it becomes dark; And even if he is in the Bet Midrash, he should leave because it is a commandment to hurry and eat (at the seder) for the children who may fall asleep, but a person should not recite Kiddush until it gets dark.
mechaber/2:main: He will arrange his table beautifully with fine dishes according to his ability, and he will prepare his seating place to recline in a dignified manner. {Rama: Even a poor person who has no cushions should sit on a bench (Mordechai, beginning of the chapter on Erev Pesach)}
mechaber/3:main: When he reclines, he should not lean on his back, nor on his face, nor on his right side, but on his left side. {Rama: (There is no distinction between a person who is lame and one who is not.}(Tur in the name of Rashi and the Tosefot, in siman 136)}
mechaber/4:main: A woman does not recline unless she is important. {Rama: (All of our women are called important, but they do not have the custom to recline because we rely on the words of the Ravyah who wrote that at that time they do not recline.)}
mechaber/5:main: A son must recline when dining with his father, even if his father is a distinguished scholar. However, a student does not need to recline before his teacher, even if the teacher is not a distinguished scholar, unless the teacher gives him permission. A great Torah scholar of his generation, even if he did not learn from him, is considered like his teacher and does not need to recline. (This is specifically when they are eating at the same table, but if the student eats at a separate table, he must recline.)
mechaber/7:main: Anyone who is required to recline, if he eats or drinks without reclining, he has not fulfilled his obligation and is required to eat and drink again while reclining. (And there are those who say that in our times where it is not customary to recline, one can rely ex post facto on the opinion of the Ravaya, that he has fulfilled his obligation without the reclining. It appears to me if he did not drink the 3rd cup or the 4th cup while reclining, he should not drink again while reclining for there is a concern that such would appear as adding on to the number of cups; however, regarding the first 2 cups he should drink again without reciting a blessing; and similarly regarding the eating of matzoh and ab initio he should recline the entire meal.)
mechaber/8:main: One must drink four cups in order; and if he drank them one after another not in order, he did not fulfill his obligation.
mechaber/9:main: The measure of the cup is a revi'it after they mix it (if he wishes to mix it), and he drinks all of it or most of it; and if there are many revi'it in it, so many people drink from it as the number of revi'it in it. And some say one must drink most of the cup even if it holds several revi'it. And one must drink the measure without a large interruption in between (Beit Yosef in the name of Rokeach).
mechaber/10:main: One who doesn't drink wine because it hurts him, or he detests it, must force himself to drink in order to fulfill the commandment of four cups
mechaber/11:main: It's a mitzvah to seek red wine {Rama: (if the white wine is not better} [Tur].}
mechaber/12:main: One fulfills the obligation with cooked wine and with confectionery
mechaber/13:main: Even a poor person who is sustained through charity must sell his clothing or sell or rent himself in order to buy wine for the four cups.
mechaber/14:main: Women are also obligated in the four cups and in all the mitzvot performed on that night.
mechaber/15:main: Children who are the age of chinuch should have a cup before him. {Rama: One should not use a cup whose lip is like that of a krug glass, since one is not able to drink a quarter-log in one sip from it. And one should also not take a cup for a cup of blessing of the Blessing over the Meal like this. ... And similarly with a cup for Kiddush.}

mishnah-berurah/9:ח: (8) (Ld) Not with a big break - that is, that he should not stay drinking most of the glass longer than to eat a reward, and if he stayed longer than this rate, the beginning of drinking does not join the end, and even in retrospect he did not come out and should go back and drink even in the last glasses [Dain is here because he adds on the glasses since he did not come out] And to begin with, one must be careful not to stay in drinking most of the glass longer than to drink a fourth to feel for the first opinion explained in the sign of the 32 And in hindsight, if he stayed in the last two cups, he will not return and drink, as explained above in siman 17, and in the first two cups, he will return and drink most of the fourth at once:
mishnah-berurah/10:א: (א) (a) Because he is hurtful, he is sorry for drinking and hurting his head, and it is not at all when he falls down from it:
mishnah-berurah/10:ב: (2) (For him) to keep unleavened bread, etc. - Masha'k on Shabbat and on good days can hear Kiddush since he is out of it, but this is the obligation of drinking on every person:
mishnah-berurah/10:ג: (ג) 4 cups (for example) and can be well merged, in fact, in which it is still worthy of sanctification (see above a sign of citation in the U.S.) and can also take boiled wine or state clay:
mishnah-berurah/11:_: (38) Red wine — for it is written "Do not look upon wine when it reddens" — evidently redness raises importance; and further, remembrance of the blood when Pharaoh slaughtered Israel. And in places where gentiles are accustomed to fabricate false libels, they refrain from taking red wine.
mishnah-berurah/12:א: (א) (Tel) comes out in boiled wine – and a better snorkel to take uncooked wine if not the maze is better and so forth
mishnah-berurah/12:ב: (ב) And in konditon — meaning mixed with honey and spices; and see above siman 272 seif 8 and what is written there — and the same applies here.
mishnah-berurah/13:א: (1) (Ma) even poor, etc. - and he who has only four glasses after pouring will drink everything for the first night. And a candle in his house is better than four cups because of the peace of his house. And the one who has only 2 and 3 glasses, see the TFG sign in MA, section 2, how should he act:
mishnah-berurah/13:ב: (ב) (b) He would sell his garments – if the eyebrows did not give him apprehension, he did not really have to break himself, they are truly committed to giving the poor four cups and achess on some places that do not keep him in mind:
mishnah-berurah/13:ג: (ג) (mg) to D. cups – of wine or a state gambler and d’ cups have been corrected against D. A.D. of redemption and I have brought you out and saved you and redeemed you and taken you:
mishnah-berurah/14:א: (א) The women also have to do so, although they are ordered that the time has been circumcised in the same miracle:
mishnah-berurah/14:ב: (ב) (What) the mitzvot and so on, such as the decree and the statement of the West:
mishnah-berurah/15:א: (א) It is a mitzvah to give, etc. — but it is not indispensable.
mishnah-berurah/15:ב: (ב) (This is) his cup before him – see the sign of the KGB in the heart that we were robbed of a small majority should not only drink as a whole of his diplomas:
mishnah-berurah/15:ג: (3) (Mah) because of etc. - and as it is explained in the sign of TAA (SA) [SO] for the matter of matzah and in retrospect it does not delay if he did not stay long and as above in Sec 34:
mishnah-berurah/15:ד: (4) (Matt.) In the Omnipresent they do not take him away - one must give his eyes to him as explained there and also regarding the matter of sanctification as in the 3rd:
mishnah-berurah/16:_: (b) And they will be asked, “Religions will arise in no way for all the subjects and practices of this night, and they will ask the questions of the introductory in the form. I will not be able to sleep and ask. And it must be aroused that we would not be married to slaves, and so that the exodus of Egypt is the answer to the question of our son, and as it is said, and that your son's religion on that day is to be preserved for it and for him (and not as much as he does, since he says what we will allow children to walk and sleep and do not know any answer to their question):
turei-zahav/1:_: until it gets dark. Damtza Domia DePesach dictating on matzoh and marori' they will eat it and Pesach is not eaten except at night and the Kiddush must be at a time appropriate for matzoh. A writer from the Rabbi from Prague in each of siman 19, who adds a dance on the holy place ACP, should have the end of the meal on the night of the third day of the day, and on the night of Hada, on the night of Daurita, and when he stops eating it before Hashich, he did not leave Dakhil, but on the night of the New Year, on the eve of Passover, the model of the Kiddush should be at night and above the taste, eating matza is in general the Kiddush and for it the Kiddush comes:
turei-zahav/3:_: Not today. Deshima will go to the deck and is on the right and the hat opens for granted that he is down to the right:
turei-zahav/4:_: This time, etc. At this time, the Prophet (PBUH) says to sab, because it is customary in our country during the rest of the year to sab, but to sit according to one's way, per the words of the Prophet, the women trust not to sab, etc., but it is not a misab because sitting in her way is the way of love, and also the custom, etc., of those who wear the kitl during the seder that they should not wear it, but it seems that the purpose of wearing the kitl is so that one's mind is not distracted from it by the joy. According to Matthew, he shall wear a garment, and in Psalm 16, the mourner shall also wear it, and Amash C.
turei-zahav/5:_: Afi' if it is not a definite rabbi. The Rash proves that it is correct in the Brei' with everything Adam Misab Efi is a student with his rabbi and my part of this is his mother, Dr. Yosef, a student of AS Hisb. And he rejected her Demeiri on the sidelines, Dangri Pi, a student of Umanu, and he didn't reject her Demeiri in a non-definite way, but from a model in which it is not definite. The permission of VL Dalshon Ha'Braith Mor' on the obligation of the rabbi and taking permission, there is no obligation on the student. Proof of this is that there is an obligation on the rabbi to give him permission. There is no Muki in the dish. It is an obligation on the rabbi to give him permission, except that this deharsha is a permission and not an obligation, as in the following:
turei-zahav/7:א: (א) And it appears to me if he did not drink, etc. — meaning that for the first two cups there is permission to drink between them and it is not like adding; and this distinction exists in Ashrei chapter Arvei Pesachim, except that he concluded on this; nevertheless one may say that since he drank not per their enactment, the matter was clarified that it was not from the number of cups, and what he drinks now is a cup of obligation; and if he drank the fourth cup without reclining he must bless borei peri hagafen on a cup he will drink afterward that he will drink with reclining — for when he drank the fourth cup without reclining and was not careful to recline, he turned his mind to drink more — until here; and so in Shulchan Aruch siman 479. One may say here on Rama: in any case, if he holds this reasoning that the matter was clarified that they were not from the number — why did he write it appears like adding to the cups, for it is not adding; and if he does not hold thus, and necessarily the reason is because b'dieved he fulfilled without reclining, for one may rely on Ravyah per the second view — if so why did he give a reason of adding, which is not necessary, for one may say the matter was clarified; he should have given a better reason, namely that since he already fulfilled with those two cups he drank without reclining, it is forbidden to drink, as we learned between third and fourth he should not drink, and similarly after the fourth he should not drink — not from concern of adding to cups, but lest he become drunk, as written siman 479. It turns out there is contradiction or abbreviation in Rama's words here.
turei-zahav/7:ב: (2) And to begin with the whole feast. KL Madai' in the Gm' of the sun who ate as a matzah olive when he was having a misav came out that another person did not go out, but one should siv at the whole meal and here I am saying that at the beginning of it he will siv at the whole meal. And in Rambam Paz 26 and Zal when is a yassab required when eating one olive of matzah and drinking four cups of these and the rest of his eating and drinking if he has a yassab then it is fine and difficult because there is no division between the shemesh and the paz. And El Deshmes A't to fulfill the mitzvah of the chosen ones, that's not the L'L'l in the sun, but the L'L''t, but to the setting, and the L'L D'in divides between the sun and the other in it, and did not take a sun there, except to teach us that even the sun is obliged to rise, and in order for the sun to pass, He allowed it for the reason, since it is necessary to go one way and the other. 20 to divide one sun into another and we will not settle for me except in the way I wrote:
turei-zahav/8:_: on order. P. As the Sages pointed out, but if you are different, it is without order that the path does not come out:
turei-zahav/9:_: All or most of it. P.M. is full of sages, or most of it in retrospect, and in countries that are expensive in the case of the Sachak, which is mostly circumcised by the K.C., and in addition to the United States
turei-zahav/11:_: After red wine. For it is written "Do not look at wine when it reddens" — learn from this that redness is an elevation; and Tur was particular here regarding the four cups with this, but not regarding kiddush in siman 472, for there is another hint to red — remembrance of the blood that Pharaoh slaughtered among Israel; and nowadays they refrain from taking red wine because of false libels among the nations.
turei-zahav/13:_: My nose is poor.
